chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The sunnah is of two (types): a sunnah pertaining to an obligation — adherence to it is guidance and its abandonment is going astray; and a sunnah pertaining to other than an obligation — adherence to it is a merit and its abandonment for [something] other is a sin.'

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: sunnah — the prophetic tradition/practice; here classified into two legally distinct types
key_terms.خَطِيئَةٌ: sin (khati'a) — a transgression; here: abandoning the non-obligatory sunnah for something else
key_terms.ضَلَالَةٌ: going astray (dalala) — misguidance, deviation from the right path
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٍ: an obligation (farida) — a divinely mandated religious duty
key_terms.هُدًى: guidance (huda) — divine direction and the correct path

ai.seo_question: What are the two types of sunnah and their rulings according to Imam Ali (AS) in al-Kafi, Chapter 22?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS), transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his blessed forefathers, classifies the prophetic sunnah into two legally distinct categories: one embedded in an obligatory act, where following it is guidance and neglecting it leads to misguidance; and one independent of any obligation, where following it earns merit and neglecting it in favor of something else constitutes a sin. This foundational teaching provides the jurisprudential framework for evaluating the moral weight of prophetic practices in Shia fiqh, distinguishing between sunnah that is integral to a fard and sunnah that is supererogatory.
